recipes.name: Ricotta Cookies
ingredients_raw: 4 cups all-purpose flour, or more as needed

steps.text: Gather the ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease or line cookie sheets.
Combine ricotta, sugar, butter, eggs, and vanilla extract in a large bowl; beat with an electric mixer until smooth and creamy.
Combine flour, baking powder, and baking soda; blend into ricotta mixture, mixing in additional flour if needed to form a workable dough.
Roll dough into walnut-sized balls and place 2 inches apart onto prepared cookie sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven until edges are golden, about 8 to 10 minutes.
To make the glaze: Mix confectioners' sugar, milk, and almond extract together until smooth. Spoon over warm cookies, and sprinkle with colored candy sprinkles.

raw_recipe.headline: Ricotta Cookies
raw_recipe.description: These Italian ricotta cookies are soft, tender, and extra delicious topped with an almond glaze and colorful candy sprinkles for a favorite holiday cookie.

video.description: Try these delicious, melt-in-your-mouth cookies that use an unlikely ingredient for a crumbly texture! In this video, Nicole shows you how to make Italian ricotta cookies with a homemade almond glaze. These tender and moist cookies are made by mixing together ricotta cream cheese with vanilla, eggs, butter, and other sweet ingredients to former the batter. After baking in the oven and with a drizzle of the almond glaze, these cookies are ready to delight at any holiday party!

review.reviewBody: I love ricotta and almond so I used all almond extract. I also refrigerated the dough for 2 hours to make it eaiser to handle. I also froze half my batch and put the frosting on after i took them out.

I am so in love these cookies! They are delicate and somewhat like little cakes with a wonderful flavor and texture. I followed the recipe very closely by keeping all ingredients the same, except for adding 1 tsp. salt and changing the extract. Instead of using 2 Tbsp. vanilla the extracts I used are; 1 tsp. vanilla, 1 tsp. almond and 1 tsp. buttery sweet dough emulsion (LorAnn brand, really yummy stuff.) I also chilled the dough and used a small cookie scoop (2.5 tsp) so there was no additional flour needed. The cold dough baked for 14 minutes and the recipe yielded 115 cookies that are about 1.5 inches across. For the glaze, after reading reviews I went ahead and doubled the amount of sugar (so 3 cups), used 1 tsp. vanilla and 1 tsp. almond and started with a 1/4 cup milk, then dribbled in more to get it to the consistency I wanted. I feel this is a very good recipe if only you use a little of your own knowledge in getting the exact flavor you want. Just use more or less almond and vanilla extracts to your liking and make the glaze as thick or thin as you want. Thank you Sandy, these cookies are wonderful!

These cookies were a breath of fresh air from the traditional cookie flavor and texture. They’re so soft and not too sweet at all. The sprinkles make it look festive. And the almond glaze on top sure makes it very appealing for especially the curious eater. You can also adjust how much glaze to add on top or even use other flavor extracts for even more variety.

These can be made Gluten Free!!! I've made them with King arthur flour called Measure for measure. It turned out tasting exactly like the non gluten version!!! I'm so happy. Also, I flash freeze the cookie dough balls on a parchment lined baking sheet. Then, once frozen, placed in a ziplock bag and store in the freezer until you want some freshly baked cookies. they taste the same! It's great! Thanks

I did add less butter by substituting applesauce for 1 stick of butter and they still came out quite good. Make sure you refrigerate the dough and use 1/2 tsp for measuring the balls. The flavor would be better with almond flavoring with the vanilla. Also, be quick to put the sprinkles because it hardens fast once you put it on the cookie.

These were very yummy cookies! Nice texture and balance of sweet. Good recipe cept... I needed another 1/2 cup of flour for my dough to come together. And it took about 20 minutes for my oven to get the cookies lightly browned. *Tip: as the dough is very sticky to work with so using a mini-ice cream scoop to form the balls makes life easier. Also, make double the amount of glaze- you will need it. I had about 100 cookies and had to whip up another batch of glaze halfway through.

Egg-free adaptation: I substitute 1 tsp of arrowroot powder and 2 Tbsp of water for each egg; therefore, use a total of 2 tsps of arrowroot powder and 4 Tbsp of water. Simply add in the arrowroot powder, followed by the water, at the step where you'd add in eggs. They turn out fine! The dough may be slightly harder to get all combined if you mix by hand. I just knead it together with my hands until it is all blended. Cookies come our fluffy and delicious!

This was a great recipe!!! But I did double the recipe as I had a 30 oz ricotta container. I will say the glaze didn't work for me so I did the glaze from Giada from food network ricotta cookie recipe, turned out much better :)
Also will be using less sugar next, they were a little sweet for me but turned out wonderful, everyone loved them!!! Side note... don't bother rolling them out the dough is too sticky. Just go buy one of those small cookie scoops and use that so much easier and you'll be happier with out all the mess on your hands and they pretty much look the same anyways.

I had so much fun making these! They are an easy family time cookie. They have a light texture and the glaze sweetness is balanced by the cookie. The cookie dough is sticky, so I used a pastry bag onto parchment paper sheets. They cooked perfectly. When we got to the fun decorating part, we opted to dip just the top of each cookie and then dipped into the colored nonpareils.

Nice tasting cookie. I didn't have a full 16 oz. of ricotta cheese so I added about 3 1/2 oz cream cheese to it and they came out just yummy. I also added an additional 1/2 cup flour since I had sifted it. I floured my hands to make the balls and it worked our fine. I may use a little less milk in the glaze next time since it really ran off. I found I needed to bake them longer 10-12 min or they came out a little underdone. and went flat when cooled. I will make again.

Absolutely the best ricotta cookies I've ever made. I upped the oven temperature to 375 for high altitude baking, and they came out in 10 minutes exactly with a wonderfully fluffy cake texture. 

By the way, I used a cookie scoop which I dipped in flour between cookies, making it extremely easy. 

The perfect use for ricotta left over from cannoli or manicotti!
I had to substitute 1/2 of the ricotta with cottage cheese, still very good! No taste difference.

This was such an easy recipe and cookies were so moist. I used a cookie scoop that was really too large so I had to cook them longer. Just kept in eye on them. But I will get a smaller scoop for the next time.

I made these for Easter and they were a big hit! I had a busy weekend so I refrigerated the dough overnight and baked them the next morning. Super easy recipe and they baked perfectly. Loved the cake-like texture and the glaze was delicious. Will definitely be making these again!

This is a simple recipe- makes a lot of pillowy soft cookies. I baked 10 minutes but next time I think 12 may be better- as I used a silpat on my cookie sheet and parchment paper as I don't like the bottoms of my cookies to get too dark. I added different pastel colors to the icing for easter colors. I'm freezing part of them as I made a double batch because I had the Ricotta cheese to use up. Cannot freeze if iced and sprinkled with non pareils as the colors will bleed on ther glaze.

Followed the cookie recipe to a T but made my glaze thicker. This pic is before I frosted them as my hubby already had four! I would advise an electric hand mixer in lieu of the KitchenAid. The latter didn't mix it well so had to dump into a large glass bowl and finish with the electric hand mixer. Awesome recipe! Thank you.

The only thing I would change is to know that walnut size is not a measurement. I had to cook them for 20 minutes. I made sure the bottoms were a bit browned so they were fully cooked. And they make a lot of cookies, I halved the batch, and I will make them smaller for the next time I make them. Otherwise, this recipe is amazing!
Instructions are NOT correct--you can't put all wet ingredients in at the same time and expect the cheese to blend.
Cookies came out great and delicious. Going to freeze them. Decorate them in a couple weeks.
